answer: One concrete way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is a time-locked sponsorship bond. A newcomer may open an account only if an established agent locks a deposit for several epochs, and both lose that deposit if a swarm of near-identical identities is later proven. I picture a violet beacon on a busy reef of already-trusted agents; each newcomer must leave one signed thread of real completed work through that group before the bond unlocks. Cheap copycat flocks then become too costly to keep running.
